My responses (please consider for the PDF we send):

1) License enumeration and classification
- For every model in the Redwood public catalog we maintain a license field and a classification tag: permissive (Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD), copyleft (GPL-family), research-only / non-commercial (e.g., certain CreativeML variants), and proprietary (third-party commercial licenses).
- The catalog CSV sample (attached) maps model_id -> upstream_license -> license_url -> license_date_recorded.

2) Exposure by license type
- Permissive licenses: available in hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Customers can use these models directly via hosted endpoints.
- Restrictive / non-commercial licenses: not exposed via our hosted multi-tenant endpoints. These are available in Dedicated pools (isolated infrastructure) or as BYOM (customer uploads the weights into their Private deployment). We flag these clearly in the catalog.
- Proprietary or redistributable-with-contract models: available subject to separate commercial terms; we include the license/contract reference in the MBOM.

3) Provenance metadata we provide
- For each model we capture and surface: upstream_repository_url, commit_hash/tag, release_date, published_paper DOI (if available), training_data_tags (high-level descriptors, not raw datasets), license_text_url, license_type, author/organization, weights_checksum (SHA256), and a unique model_fingerprint (internal UUID + version tag).
- Example fields are included in model-provenance-sample.csv attached.

4) Version pinning and reproducibility guarantees
- Every model offered has a model_id (e.g., llm-redwood:vicuna-13b:20240201) which is immutable once published. Customers can request pinned endpoints (hosted or Dedicated) which will route to the specific model_id.
- For Dedicated customers we provide version-freeze periods (configurable) and snapshot exports of weights + KV-cache dump for full reproducibility under contract. Hosted customers receive version pinning by model_id but do not receive weight exports; we guarantee API stability for the pinned model_id for a minimum SLA window (typical enterprise term: 90 days post-deprecation notice) or per contract.

5) License changes and remediation
- If upstream license or provenance changes, we treat this as a catalog update event. We notify impacted customers via the Console, email, and the HubSpot record. For Hosted customers: we will attempt to provide a functionally-equivalent replacement and, where not possible, offer migration assistance or a Dedicated/BYOM path.
- For enterprise contracts we include explicit remediation timelines and escalation paths; legal will advise on notes required in the MSA.

6) MBOM and audits
- We produce a machine-readable MBOM (CSV/JSON) per model which includes the fields above and the transitive license graph for major dependencies.
- We support license audits: for Hosted customers we provide MBOM exports and documented provenance metadata. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can provide broader audit evidence (checksums, internal logs) under NDA.

7) Other controls
- Export control & sanctions: models are reviewed for dual-use/export risk; we will flow-down export control clauses in enterprise agreements and refuse hosting for models where export restrictions apply unless customer-specific controls are in place.
- Takedown & DMCA: we have a documented takedown process; customers are notified and we support forensic evidence collection when required.

Rishi / Neha — quick legal notes to add into the customer-facing PDF:

- License compliance: Redwood uses a combined approach — we track upstream license metadata and we operate automated scanners for license text/manifest. Final compliance responsibility for customer use of model outputs follows the upstream license and the customer's own obligations; Redwood disclaims indemnity for customer content that is user-derived unless specifically contracted.
- Indemnity & liability: we can offer limited representations about license accuracy in the catalog (e.g., "to the best of our knowledge as of the recorded date"). Any stronger reps/warranties require negotiation and are typically limited to Dedicated or Private tiers.
- Audits & evidence: we will provide MBOM exports and provenance artifacts under NDA. For Hosted customers a forensic export (weights) is not available — for those needs customers should consider Dedicated/Private.
- License change: we will notify customers within 5 business days of a material upstream license change that affects availability; remediation timelines will be defined per contract (standard: 30 days for migration assistance unless immediate block required).
- Export controls / sanctions: add a clause that Redwood will comply with applicable export control laws and will not permit hosting of models that violate sanction regimes; customers must certify the end use where required.

I recommend we add a short paragraph in the PDF summarizing what is "available via hosted API" vs "requires Dedicated/BYOM" and flag typical contractual addenda (license accuracy rep, audit support, export controls).
